# Sage secures $65M to scale AI monitoring platform for aging population
[Investing](https://www.mobihealthnews.com/enterprise-taxonomy-topic/investing)

Senior care technology platform [Sage](https://www.mobihealthnews.com/tag/sage) has raised $65 million in Series C funding, led by Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, bringing its total raise to $124 million.

The company will use the funds to enhance its technology, including deepening investments in its predictive AI offerings around resident safety, caregiver workflow and skilled nursing.

"This investment allows us to put caregivers at the center of innovation – by delivering a platform that provides real-time intelligence, and by convening an inaugural summit to ensure their voices and expertise drive the future of the industry," Raj Mehra, cofounder and CEO of Sage, said in a statement.

In 2024, Sage secured $35 million in Series B funding, one year after raising [$15 million in a Series A funding round](https://www.mobihealthnews.com/news/senior-care-platform-sage-secures-15m-and-more-digital-health-fundings). The company garnered [$9 million in seed funding](https://www.mobihealthnews.com/news/diagnostic-robotics-raises-45m-ai-enabled-care-management-and-more-digital-health-fundings) in 2022.

### NIA’s AI for Dementia Competition
The NIA funds the a2 Pilot Awards through three AITCs at Johns Hopkins University, the University of Massachusetts-Amherst, and the University of Pennsylvania, with coordination support provided by Rose Li & Associates, Inc. Pilot applicants can request **up to $200,000 in non-dilutive direct costs** to be expended within a 12-month period, with multi-year commitments and time extensions determined by the awarding AITC.
